recipes.name: Cream of Asparagus Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 pound fresh asparagus, trimmed and cut into 1 inch pieces

steps.text: Combine asparagus, 1/2 cup chicken broth, and onion in a large saucepan; cover and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer, uncovered, until asparagus is tender, about 12 minutes. Transfer the mixture to a blender; puree until smooth and set aside.
In the same saucepan, melt butter over medium-low heat. Stir in flour, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes.
Increase heat to medium; add remaining chicken broth, stirring constantly, until the mixture boils. Stir in pureed asparagus and milk.

Place sour cream in a small bowl and stir in a ladleful of hot soup until blended; pour into the soup and stir in lemon juice. Warm soup through to serving temperature, without boiling. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Cream of Asparagus Soup
raw_recipe.description: This asparagus soup is super easy to make with fresh asparagus, broth, sour cream, and a squeeze of lemon for a creamy, silky smooth spring soup.

video.description: This bright and creamy soup will liven up any meal!

review.reviewBody: This is the best asparagus soup I've ever tasted, and I order it in many fine restaurants. Ignore everyone who has reviewed this recipe without making this recipe verbatum and tell you to add bacon, lettuce, tomato, potato, wine, rubbing alcohol, peanuts, pork, lighter fluid, etc etc. If they never followed the recipe, they shouldn't be reviewing it. Make it exactly as described and you won't be disappointed. After making it the first time, go ahead and add some chocolate chips or pine cones or whatever you think it needs, but review it based upon this recipe. It's a winner!

This was so tasty we ran out and bought asparagus so we could make more! Remember that you can use the big asparagus that you wouldn't use otherwise because it's going to be pureed. Other than doubling the recipe the only thing I would change is that I would save the asparagus heads after sauteeing and use them as garnish instead of pureeing them. Excellent recipe!

This was a great recipe to start with but I added a few things;
I fried *bacon and removed it from the pot then added asparagus, *garlic, *leek and onions and *sauteed for about five minutes before adding the stock to simmer. I also added *1/2 cup white wine to the stock.

As a garnish, I sauteed the asparagus spears in olive oil.

It was a very easy, fun and delicious soup to make. I can't wait to make it again.

* = my changes to the recipe

Who knew that starting out with doggie bag asparagus from our dinner out the other night would end up creating something so delicious and elegant?! Because I was using asparagus already cooked crisp/tender I had to modify the cooking method a bit and I improvised on the recipe to a minor degree as well, but not so much as to significantly alter the intent of the recipe. I used half and half rather than the milk and sour cream and an equal measure of chicken broth. I also substituted shallots for the onion. I liked that this recipe limited itself to the clean and simple flavor of the asparagus, without distracting additions of garlic or other seasonings and it proved itself out. I made this ahead of time and it was easy enough to reheat once I was ready to serve dinner. To garnish, I sauteed scallops in browned butter, nestled one in each soup bowl, then topped the scallop with criss-crossed asparagus tips. Because of our frequent and extensive travel, hubs and I eat at wonderful restaurants all over the country, and we both declared this soup as fine as we've had anywhere.

This was wonderful! Asparagus is in season near me, so instead of throwing out the end pieces, I boil about 4 pounds of them until tender then put in a food processor with a little liquid. Afterwards, push through a sieve and discard the woody stringy parts. This works fabulously, repurposing the end pieces instead of using a pound of asparagus. I then cut up 6 or so pieces of cooked asparagus and add it at the very end with the lemon juice. If it doesn't seem thick enough, I add a whisked flour/milk mixture to desired consistency.

This soup is fantastic! The only thing I did differently was sautéing the onion in a little oil to carmelize them a bit....then adding a bit of white wine to deglaze the pan. I shoved the onions to the side of the pan to whisk together the melted butter and flour. I added the chopped asparagus later after the broth came to a simmer. I also didn’t measure the fresh lemon juice at the end. I just juiced half of a lemon and added that. The fresh lemon really brightens this soup and adds a remarkable flavor. Try not to use bottled lemon juice if you have a choice. A hand held immersion blender created a perfect texture with a few larger pieces here and there. If you like to make soups it’s a kitchen “gadget“ well worth having. This soup came together quickly and I will make it again and again. Thank you!

Really excellent soup! I did a few things different though…. I steamed the asparagus and saved out a few of the tips for garnish. I sautéed the onion with a clove of garlic in a bit of butter. Then I puréed all those ingredients together. After making the roux and thickening the broth, I added a corn starch slurry because I like an extra thick I soup. I also used just a 1/2 tsp of salt and a 1/4 tsp of pepper. The garlic, pepper and lemon juice go together so well. I served in heated bowls and topped the soup with asparagus tips and a few croutons. My husband said it was the fanciest soup he ever tasted!

I've made this soup a number of times. It's always so good. I cut the tops of the asparagus off and steamed them separately so that I could garnish the soup after it was finished. I usually use more asparagus than the recipe calls for. Make sure you use the lemon juice as it really brightens up the flavor and is super delicious!

Wow….Outstanding flavor..thanks for this one. Substitutions: 1). Used two large cloves fresh garlic added the last few minutes of cooking the asparagus and onions.(.in place of powdered garlic) 2). Used 3/4 cup heavy whipping cream with 1/4 cup cold water. (In place of milk) 3). Organic yogurt in place of sour cream. Served with fresh sour dough bread toasted with butter..👍🏻👍🏻

Actually , this is fairly good as written. I gave it only 4 stars b/c I feel it NEEDS more seasoning. I made this in the early spring, when fresh asparagus was just starting to come out.

 2nd time I made this I used low sodium chicken stock in a box, Added a scant teaspoon ish teaspoon of dried thyme leaves ( GROUND would be less) And 2 lg fresh garlic cloves minced. Plus a good couple of twists of cracked pepper. To the flour, i added a pinch of garlic powder, a pinch of penzys dried shallot powder ( awsome stuff) The added seasoning made it much better for my taste., and worthy of 5 stars
One thing I did notice is that reviews who used vegetable stock, reported a bland taste review.. A tip for or clarity, I think the directions should read " temper in some hot broth, a bit at a time into the room temp sour cream, before adding to the soup" . Personally, I just serve sour cream on the side, and use half & half in place of milk. Or just use whole milk .
Absolutely delicious. Used homemade chicken stock. Make sure to follow instructions for the techniques. Especially important to brown the flour and seasonings in butter.
Made this soup without changing a thing. It was so delicious! Even better than what you order in the restaurant. I'll definitely be making this again.
I use half-n-half instead of milk for a thicker consistency.
Easy and accurate. You can make minor adjustments to the recipe and it turns out terrific. My adult children demand I prepare this when they visits. Yes. A keeper.
It was ok I guess. A good way to use asparagus but didn't care for it too much. Probably wouldn't make a second time.
One of my favorite soups! And, it can be doubled, halved.....whatever you want depending on the amount of asparagus you have. My leftover is always used for soup.
Made as written except doubled everything but the salt. Devine!
Hubby is in love with it! I make it a couple times a month!
Delicious!!!!

Made this soup a few times. Love it. A few changes. I add bacon. Cook the tops of the asparagus in the pan where the bacon was cooked to add them as a garnish to eat bowl. Changed the milk to coconut milk. A few chilli pepper flakes. And leave out the sour scream as the coconut milk makes is pretty cream. Oh and of course double it and it’s a favourite
